findings: Opaque white/light checkerboard patches remain in open spaces between weight-stack rails, beneath the machine base and inside bench support openings. Female frames 0, 2 and 3 also retain large white gaps behind the lower legs; frames 2 and 3 have white behind the neck/ponytail. These stay white against the dark background.

Male frame 0 changes the tower geometry and bench/athlete placement relative to frames 1-3. Female frame 1 shifts the entire bench, tower and planted feet right relative to frames 0, 2 and 3, and its darker rendering/cleaner interior transparency produces a visible flicker. These stationary equipment changes are separate from intended arm movement.
Male frame 0 is shirtless; frames 1–3 have a black tank top. This creates a conspicuous wardrobe change during animation.

Stationary cable towers change design, base shape, pulley arrangement, spacing and perspective across both sequences. Female frame 3 has stacked top pulleys whereas earlier frames have a single top pulley; frame 2 has distinctly different outward feet. These changes cannot be explained by the athlete's arm movement and cause visible equipment morphing.
Female frames 0–1 place the image-right foot forward, while frames 2–3 place the image-left foot forward. The staggered stance switches abruptly during the cable pull without an intervening step.

White background remains inside enclosed gaps: male 1 near the lower hand/rope and torso, male 2 between arm/rope and torso, female 0 between neck and ponytail, female 1 in small arm/torso gaps, and most prominently female 2 in the triangular gap between upper arm and torso. These stay white on the dark preview; female 2 is conspicuous at sequence size.
Thin pale fringe is visible along portions of athlete and equipment contours on dark backgrounds. Illustrations remain usable, with no severe clipping or missing limbs observed.

The cable-machine base and upright shift and change apparent size across each sequence, especially frame 0 versus later frames. Athlete bending and arm rotation are genuine motion, but machine movement introduces limited animation jitter.
An opaque white wedge fills the enclosed gap between bent forearms, upper arm and face. It remains white on the dark background and visibly flashes relative to neighboring frames.

White slivers remain between the neck/back of head and bench; the female set has a wider white wedge under the head and ponytail. These do not adopt the dark background. The narrow male remnants are less prominent.

Tall enclosed areas between the cable-tower rails remain opaque white/light gray on the dark background; faint checker texture is particularly visible in female frame 0. Female frames 0 and 1 also retain white fill inside the handle and ponytail/neck gap.

Male frame 3 shifts both athlete and stationary tower substantially left relative to frames 0–2 (roughly 100 pixels), with a lower head and pulley top while feet/base remain near the previous baseline. This creates a visible animation jump unrelated to elbow extension.
Disconnected thin vertical light segments remain far to the right of the cable tower in male frame 3.
Female tower shifts horizontally across the sequence, most noticeably to the right in frame 3, while the athlete remains approximately anchored. Smaller body contour/foot changes are also visible.

Both sequences increase elbow flexion and raise the handle from frame 0 to 3, but the selected weight block descends in the male sequence. In the female sequence it first rises at frame 1, then drops markedly in frames 2 and 3 while the handle continues upward. The stack also changes apparent thickness, particularly in female frame 3. These conspicuous equipment changes undermine the cable mechanism's animation coherence.

Large opaque white/checkerboard regions remain between the legs and within both cable towers, plus pale residue around feet and equipment bases. Both frame-0 images retain white between raised arms; male frame 1 has white wedges beside the neck; male frame 2 has a large checkerboard triangle between cables and arms. These stand out strongly on dark backgrounds.

Cable paths visually disappear behind the neck/shoulder or upper arms rather than visibly reaching the held handles (male 1 and 3, female 2). Routing switches between crossed and uncrossed across the sequences. Review the intended cable-to-handle connection and exercise motion; the depicted routing is inconsistent.
Tower bases and frame geometry shift between poses, most visibly at frame 2 in both sequences, despite the equipment being stationary. Athlete identity and overall scale remain broadly consistent.

Opaque white and baked checkerboard patches remain beneath the bench, between the legs, in the arm/torso gaps, and along the floor boundary. Male frame 3 has a partially transparent under-bench region but conspicuous checker squares and other filled gaps. Residue visibly changes between frames and is especially obvious on dark backgrounds.
Small white specks remain beneath and between the bench and shoes, with a fine light fringe around portions of the outline. The large under-bench region is transparent in this frame.

Stationary bench and cable-machine boundaries shift modestly across both sequences; machine position and bench/foot baseline are not fully registered. Movement of the hands and forearms is distinct from this limited equipment drift.

Opaque white background remains in the enclosed space between raised arms and head in every frame. It stays white on the dark preview instead of revealing the background, and becomes a large conspicuous wedge in extended-arm frames. White enclosed patches also appear near the machine base; bright vertical rails may partly be intended metal highlights.
The stationary cable tower changes height and base position across the female sequence while the feet remain approximately anchored. This produces visible equipment drift unrelated to elbow movement.
Numerous bright white irregular patches remain in the open cable-machine interior above and below the raised weight stack, conspicuous on dark backgrounds.
Small white remnants are visible in machine openings, particularly around the top crossbar and lower base/weight-stack gaps.

Stationary shoe positions and machine uprights shift horizontally between frames. The shifts are limited but would cause visible drift in a fixed-canvas animation; arm movement and weight-stack travel are expected motion.
The machine top crossbar meets the upper canvas boundary with no padding; the top edge appears slightly clipped. The exercise remains understandable.

Opaque white patches remain in enclosed equipment gaps: below the male weight stack and in female machine uprights; white handle interiors are especially visible in male 0/2/3 and female frames. Female 0/1 also have a white neck-to-ponytail gap. These areas remain white on the dark composite.
Light fringe/residue follows shoe soles and machine base; a conspicuous ragged light strip lies below the ball in female 0, with thinner strips in female 2/3.

Frame 0 handle cable points off image-left although the depicted machine is on image-right. In frames 1-3 the handle cable attaches toward the right machine. Male 0 also shows a separate cable behind the torso toward the right pulley. The resistance connection switches sides across the sequence.
Leftmost shoe toe meets and is slightly cut by the left canvas boundary in female 0/2/3.
Opaque pale gray/white ground-shaped remnant bridges the area beneath the shoes and extends toward the bench base. It is conspicuous against the dark background and absent from the other frames.

Stationary bench and cable tower shift horizontally between frames, especially female 0 to 1 to 2; bench width and tower placement vary modestly. This is separate from the intended torso flexion and moving weight stack.
Thin pale rough outlines are visible around portions of the athlete, cable and equipment on the dark background. Female frame 0 also has speckled residue inside the upper tower's open rail area.

The forefeet appear separated from the fixed sloping footplate: male frame 1 shows a clear gap in front of the toes, and female frame 3 raises the shoes above/behind the plate with block-like supports appearing beneath the heels. This makes the calf-press load/contact relationship unclear and changes the equipment depiction between phases.
Small background-colored pinholes interrupt the solid lower front curved base rail and a horizontal machine crossbar. They turn black on the dark preview and light on the light preview.

Irregular elongated transparent patches cut through the solid silver diagonal rails (and smaller upper rail highlights). These patches become black on dark backgrounds and light on light backgrounds, visibly eroding the equipment.
Thin ragged pale residue remains beneath and inside the lower machine base, with light edge fringe elsewhere; most visible on the dark background.

The stationary seat, base corners and rear storage plate shift slightly between frames in both sequences. This is distinct from intended footplate and leg motion; the overall machine remains recognizable and similarly scaled.

Both variants consistently wear off-white sleeveless tops and navy/white shorts, departing substantially from the README's charcoal-black training kit with restrained muted-red accents. The hand-drawn rendering and within-variant identity are otherwise consistent.

Male frame 1 slightly enlarges the stationary rack and shifts its base lower relative to frames 0 and 2; rack width and foot anchor change together, indicating a small framing/scale pulse rather than calf movement alone.

Opaque white triangular interiors remain inside band handles, most conspicuous in male frames 0 and 3 and female frame 0. Male frame 0 also has long white strips between the bands and trouser legs; female frame 0 has white wedges between the arms and waist. These remain white against the dark background and are enclosed background residue.

Male frames 0/1 versus 2/3 change face/hair rendering, torso shape, shirt hem height, trouser length and shoe proportions noticeably. Head and bottom framing remain fixed while the body is redrawn, producing a visible discontinuity beyond the intended heel raise.
All eight frames use white sleeveless tops and light-gray trousers, departing substantially from the README specification of charcoal-black training kit with muted-red accents.
A large opaque white enclosed background patch remains between the legs, extending from below the shorts to the shoes. It is conspicuous on the dark composite.

Thin pale dotted/fringed outlines remain along portions of the athlete contours, especially hair, arms, legs and shoe edges on dark backgrounds. These are limited edge artifacts rather than large exterior background regions.

Broad white/gray ground remnants sit below the hips and along the roller underside in all male frames, with smaller remnants by hands. Frame 2 has a detached strip under the raised hips. These stand out on dark backgrounds and change shape across the sequence.
Thin light edging follows portions of hair, body, clothing and roller contours, most visible against dark backgrounds.

Thin pale outlines remain along portions of the cutout, especially enclosed arm/leg and handle gaps and equipment edges. Visible on dark backgrounds; no large opaque background patches or substantial cutout holes observed.

Female bent-pose frames 1 and 2 have visibly enlarged head, torso and tire proportions relative to standing frames 0 and 3. The head enlargement and changing tire size exceed the expected vertical displacement from bending, producing conspicuous scale changes in the ordered sequence.

Opaque white/light background islands remain inside the bent-arm/torso gap: image-left arm in male 0, 1, 3; image-right arm in male 2 and female 0, 1. These are clearly visible against the dark background. Male 1 also has a small light island between the legs.
Thin pale fringe around portions of hair and body/clothing contours is visible against the dark background; more conspicuous around male hair and the female ponytail. Figures remain otherwise intact.

Opaque white or pale checkerboard interiors remain between the arms. Male 2/3 and female 0/1 have substantial panels; female 2/3 retain smaller triangular panels. These contrast strongly on dark backgrounds and change shape across the sequence.
Small white wedges remain between overlapping lower legs/shoes; a fine pale fringe is visible along portions of the silhouette, especially hair and clothing on dark backgrounds.
Large opaque white/light checker-textured wedge remains between the arms and torso above the ball, conspicuous on the dark background.

Release-frame athletes are substantially smaller than frames 0–2: head, torso, legs and shoes shrink together while the released ball occupies upper canvas space. This is a scale discontinuity beyond the legitimate overhead reach and throwing motion.
Small light triangular residue extends behind the image-right shoe; thin pale edging is also visible on the dark preview.

Large white or faint checkerboard-filled regions remain between the raised/bent arms and handles, beside the head and hanging chains, and between lower legs and bench supports. These remain pale on the dark background rather than revealing it. Small white wedges also remain between torso/head and bench. The exterior is transparent, but interior background removal is incomplete.

The stationary bench and planted feet move rightward and the bench changes apparent length/position across indices 0 to 3 in both variants. This is distinct from the intended elbow extension and creates visible animation drift.
Opaque white/light checkerboard fill remains in the open gap between the raised arms and handle, conspicuous on the dark background.
White wedges remain between the head/neck and bench; female frames also retain white background inside the enclosed ponytail gap. Thin pale contour fringes are visible on dark backgrounds.

Male frame 0 changes bench perspective, leg placement, handle orientation and gray rather than red clothing trim relative to frames 1–3. Frame 3 substantially shrinks the athlete and bench and moves the bench lower relative to frames 1–2; stationary anchors visibly jump independently of the press motion.
Female frames 2–3 shift bench and head position and slightly change scale relative to 0–1, causing visible stationary-bench movement through the sequence.
Isolated thin vertical stray marks remain near the left upper edge and right middle edge, separate from the illustration.

Opaque white/light checkerboard patches remain in the open areas beneath the chair seat and between the image-right arm and torso. These enclosed backgrounds are conspicuous on dark backgrounds; checkerboard squares are especially clear in male frame 1 and female frames 1–2.

Chair, planted foot and torso shift horizontally across frames despite the seated knee-extension motion. Male frame 3 is noticeably farther right than frame 0; female frame 2 is farther right than the surrounding frames. This will create visible sliding during animation.
The top of the female frame 3 hairstyle touches and is slightly cut by the top canvas boundary, unlike the other female frames which retain a small margin.

Irregular opaque white/light-gray patches remain under and between the shoes and around chair feet, strongly visible on dark backgrounds. Thin light edge fringe is also visible around body and equipment contours.
The image-left shoe toe is abruptly truncated along a vertical interior cut line in both return frames, despite unused transparent canvas to its left.
Chair and foot anchors shift slightly across each sequence, most noticeably on the return to upright in frame 3. Torso bending and ponytail movement are expected exercise movement.
Opaque pale gray/white floor-shaped patches remain between and behind the shoes and machine feet. They stand out clearly on the dark background instead of blending with transparency.

The stationary machine changes height/scale across the squat sequence. Frame 2 has a markedly shorter rack; the male sequence also shifts the machine and foot baseline downward. Squat motion does not explain changes in the stationary rack.
Detached pieces resembling a second rack top appear at the bottom canvas edge, separated from the main complete illustration.
Broad opaque pale gray/white jagged floor patches remain under and between the shoes and chair legs, conspicuous on dark backgrounds.
The image-left shoe is abruptly cut off along a vertical internal boundary in frames 2 and 3, despite available transparent canvas.
A detached shoe-like fragment floats to the right near floor level in both frame-2 images.
Small skin-colored triangular fragment below the feet in male frames 0 and 3.
Chair and planted feet shift between frames; frame 2 is displaced left relative to frames 0 and 1, with smaller position changes on the return. Torso bending itself is intended movement.
Raised fingertips end at a flat horizontal cutoff in female frames 0 and 3.

Return frame has an abrupt vertical cutoff through the image-left hand/bar end despite ample transparent canvas beyond it. The male hand is visibly truncated; both variants lose the left orange bar cap seen in frame 0.

Irregular opaque white/light-gray patches extend beyond shoe soles onto the surrounding transparent ground; thin pale edge fringe is also visible against dark backgrounds. These are limited artifacts, not a full opaque background.
A small isolated orange bar-cap-like fragment floats to the right of the torso at waist height while the actual bar is overhead.

Opaque pale gray/white ground remnants form jagged, blocky strips beneath shoes, knee and ball. Detached flecks and squared edges are conspicuous on dark backgrounds and inconsistent with a transparent shadow.
An extraneous partial ball appears to the right behind the athlete, in addition to the released ball in front. It terminates at an abrupt vertical edge inside the canvas.
The thrown ball is truncated by a straight vertical cut within the canvas, leaving an incomplete ball floating beside the extended hands despite available canvas margin.
Thin light fringe follows portions of hair, clothing and limbs, visible against dark background.

Release frames have a hard vertical internal cut near x=212 through the rear shoe/foot and ground patch, despite unused transparent canvas to the left. Female rear shoe is mostly absent; male shoe is truncated.
Detached partial shoe appears near x=790 at ground level, far to the right of the otherwise complete kneeling figure.

Grounded knees and rear foot translate markedly left from setup through extension/release and jump right on return, by roughly 100-150 pixels across the sequence. Ball/arm travel is appropriate movement, but this translation of the planted lower body creates obvious animation drift.
Small isolated light sliver near x=790 at ground level to the right of the figure.
Thin pale contour fringe is visible around portions of hair, clothing, ball and shoes on the dark background.

Broad opaque pale gray/white floor remnants remain beneath the ball, knees and planted hand. Jagged cutout edges and disconnected/blocky patches are especially evident on dark backgrounds; these are not clean transparent shadows.

Artwork has abrupt vertical cutoffs inside the transparent canvas: male frame 1 truncates the rear shoe at the right; male frame 3 and female frames 1–3 truncate the left ball contour, with female frame 3 also cutting the hand at that boundary. These are source-art cutoffs rather than preview cropping.

The ball changes apparent size/position across each sequence, particularly female frame 3 versus frames 0–2; the return pose does not align with the starting ball contour. Torso lowering and arm flexion are genuine movement and are not classified as jitter.

Opaque white/light patches remain in enclosed negative space between arms, head and bar, and between the legs. Male frame 0 also shows faint checkerboard pattern in the large overhead gap. These patches stand out on dark backgrounds.

Rack width increases relative to frame 0, while the top bar drops in later frames (most clearly male frame 3); rack peg spacing and placement also change. The stationary rack visibly reshapes across the ordered sequence, independently of the athlete's upward motion.

Opaque white/light checkerboard remains in enclosed gaps between the hanging arm and torso/thigh. Male frame 0 also has a white patch between the legs above the dumbbell; male frame 1 has a white patch above the bell between the legs. These stay white on the dark background.

Both sequences visibly shrink the athlete to fit the overhead position. Bent setup frames have much larger heads, shoes and body widths than the overhead frames; male frame 2 to 3 also clearly reduces shoe and head size. This exceeds pose-related changes and creates a zoom jump despite similar floor level.

Thin pale fringes are visible along portions of the silhouette on dark backgrounds. Female frame 0 additionally has scattered residual pixels along the floor between the shoes and ragged pale edges around the shoes.

Female setup/lift frames 0 and 1 show broad flat cylindrical dumbbell ends, while rack and overhead frames 2 and 3 use spherical circus-bell ends. The equipment design changes noticeably within the sequence.

Opaque white/light checkerboard remains in enclosed background gaps. Male 0 has a large checkerboard patch beneath shorts and beside knees; male 1 retains patches between forearms and knees; male 2 has large white areas between arms and torso. Female 0 and 1 retain large white/light checkerboard areas between arms, torso and legs above the bar. These remain visible on dark backgrounds.

Both frontal sequences change equipment scale: the barbell is nearly canvas-wide in frames 0 and 1, then substantially shorter with smaller plates in frame 2. Female frame 3 enlarges it again. Athlete head/body scale also varies. This produces visible zoom-like changes beyond the intended vertical pull and catch movement; foot baseline remains broadly stable.

Thin light and intermittently jagged outlines are visible around portions of the athletes and equipment on dark backgrounds. The illustrations remain readable; no substantial interior checkerboard or clothing holes were seen.
Male frame 3 has detached vertical dash-like marks near the right canvas edge. Female frame 1 has small detached flecks above the right weight plate.

Both final overhead frames shrink the barbell substantially compared with frames 0–2 (roughly from almost full canvas width to about three quarters), accompanied by smaller head/body scale. Male frame 3 also shifts left. This creates a conspicuous zoom/position discontinuity beyond the expected arm lift and split-stance motion.

Opaque white/light checkerboard patches remain between arms and torso/legs in every frame, including beneath the bent arms in frame 3. These contrast strongly against the dark background; female frame 2 also retains a small white patch above the bar between the shorts.

Barbell width and plate size shrink markedly from setup to later frames in both sequences, despite a fixed frontal viewpoint. Male head/body scale also drops between frames 1 and 2 while head top and soles remain nearly anchored. These are scale changes beyond the intended rising pull motion.
Male frame 0 is bald; frames 1–3 have short dark hair. This conspicuous identity change is unrelated to curling motion.
Female frames 0–1 wear a full-length top covering the abdomen; frames 2–3 abruptly change to a cropped top exposing the abdomen, including in the lowered return pose.
Gray opaque patches/fringe extend beyond both shoes in starting frames, especially broad gray islands beside the female shoes. These patches disappear in subsequent frames.
Thin pale fringe and intermittent light specks trace portions of athlete, bench and plates, visible on dark backgrounds. Limited perimeter artifact; artwork remains usable.
Female frame 1 has a small opaque light triangle between hands/forearms and chest; female frame 2 has a small light patch beneath the neck above the bench. These remain light on the dark composite.

From female frame 0 to frames 1–3 the bench, torso and planted feet shift up and right visibly. The bench feet move roughly 40–60 source pixels; this stationary equipment jump is separate from the intended bar/arm movement and harms animation continuity.
Male bench/head anchors drift modestly between frames; frame 3 bench sits higher. In both variants the red shoulder/upper-arm highlighting appears after frame 0, creating a color discontinuity.

Stationary machine and bench change viewpoint, geometry, width and anchor positions between frames. Male frame 2 is substantially wider and more frontal than frame 0; female frames likewise change bench supports, tower configuration and perspective. These changes would cause obvious animation jumps beyond the intended arm/weight-stack motion.
Gray opaque ground-like patches and edge residue remain beneath shoes and around machine feet, most conspicuous in female frame 3 on the dark background.
Top pulley/beam has a flat horizontal cutoff with padding above it, unlike the rounded fully visible pulley in the other frames. Athlete and grip remain visible.
Enclosed gaps between arms and torso retain opaque white/light checkerboard areas, conspicuous on the dark background.
Pale ground patches/fragments remain below shoes and dumbbell bases. Especially broad oval patches appear in female frames 0 and 2; other frames have smaller irregular fringes.

Stationary dumbbell and foot anchors shift across the sequence, with visibly changing dumbbell/body scale. Male frame 0 has a bare muscle-highlighted chest whereas later frames introduce a black tank top; female abdominal highlighting disappears by frame 3. These appearance changes and anchor drift create animation discontinuities beyond the expected elbow/torso movement.
Male frame 2 switches from short sleeves to sleeveless and has different face/shoe rendering.
Both sequences enlarge the character between extended and tucked poses; ground/contact placement shifts.
Male frame 2 floats above a detached pale oval shadow.

Equipment changes construction between frames: plate size/count, pivot support and elbow cradle vary; the female frame 1 beam becomes a rectangular rail, while the other frames use a round shaft. The stationary base also shifts substantially across each sequence. These changes exceed walking/rotation motion and cause visible morphing and anchor jumps.
Small ragged brown/dark residue beneath the plates and around the base is visible on the light background.

Opaque white/light-gray checkerboard remains in enclosed arm-to-torso gaps in all eight frames, with additional retained background in bench openings and between legs in several frames. These patches are conspicuous on the dark background.

Bench changes from a simple open rectangular support in frames 0 and 3 to a perforated cross-brace construction in frames 1 and 2 in both variants. Bench length, orientation, supports and foot anchors shift visibly, beyond the expected movement of a seated curl. Male frame 0 also has a noticeably smaller overall figure than subsequent frames.
Thin pale contour flecks occur around portions of hair, footwear and bench edges on dark backgrounds; female frames 1 and 3 have especially visible light residue beneath bench feet.

A broad opaque pale-gray ground oval appears beneath both feet in frames 1–3 of each gender but is absent in frame 0. It is conspicuous on the dark background and switches on/off at the sequence boundary.
Thin pale fringes trace portions of hair, arms, legs and equipment on dark backgrounds in frames 1–3.
Detached light specks float above and to image-right of the athlete; a small bright fragment also borders the image-left arm.
Clothing and skin acquire a visibly rougher mottled texture compared with the smooth frame 0 illustrations, especially female frames 1–3 and male frames 2–3.
Thin pale edging is visible along portions of the cutout on dark backgrounds, especially enclosed leg/ball gaps. Illustrations remain usable.
Detached thin pale horizontal and elliptical strokes remain beneath the athlete and ball in male frame 0.

Female sequence shifts the ball and lower-body ground anchors upward in frames 2 and 3 versus 0 and 1. The ball bottom rises visibly (roughly 70 source pixels by frame 3), while its size also varies. This produces a floating/bobbing support rather than solely a torso crunch.

Male overhead frame 3 has a substantially smaller head, torso and legs than frames 1–2 while the feet remain near the same baseline. The standing athlete visibly shrinks to accommodate raised arms; this is not explained by the press movement.
Male frame 0 shows a much longer bar and larger-diameter plates than subsequent frames. The frontal barbell changes apparent size abruptly between setup and the first action phase.

Female overhead frame 3 reduces the head-to-feet body scale relative to the preceding standing frames, with a lower head and shorter legs despite straight knees and a similar foot baseline. This introduces visible shrinkage in the sequence.

Opaque white and faint checkerboard patches remain in enclosed negative spaces between bent arm and torso and between crossed legs in all eight frames. Female frame 1 also has white residue between ponytail and neck. These patches remain white on the dark preview and materially disrupt transparent display.
Thin pale perimeter fringe is visible against dark backgrounds around portions of hair, arms, shoes and lower outlines.

In both variants, bent-leg frames 0 and 3 have visibly larger heads and upper bodies than extended-leg frames 1 and 2. The head/shoulders shift substantially rightward and the back shifts upward in extended poses, while the artwork continues to fill nearly the whole canvas width. Limb extension is intended movement, but changing head size and translating the resting torso are not explained by that movement and will cause a pronounced animation jump.

Both sequences keep the head near the same top edge while the athlete bends, visibly enlarging the torso, thighs and barbell in frames 1 and especially 2 relative to standing frame 0. Plate diameter and bar span change substantially. Foot spacing and floor anchors also shift, producing size/perspective popping rather than only a hinge motion.

Band and plate construction changes between frames: male frame 1 right band ends abruptly beside the floor patch without a visible return/anchor; female frame 1 right band attaches inside the plate, while frame 2 wraps over the plate face. Male frame 3 changes from smooth solid plates to spoke/recessed plates. These discontinuities materially disrupt equipment continuity.

A narrow opaque pale oval/strip remains beneath the feet and bands in every frame, conspicuous on dark backgrounds. It may be an authored ground shadow, but reads as a light platform rather than a transparent shadow.
